title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is Grothendieck's genus-1 'loop equation' material (the Teichmüller tower in genus 0 and 1, continuing La Longue Marche). The notation is not fully defined on this page, so the following identifications are inferred from the orders and the neighbouring pages.

- 𝔊 = GL(2,ℤ).
- 𝔊[4] = the level-4 principal congruence subgroup, so 𝔊/𝔊[4] = GL(2,ℤ/4).
- Π_0 ⊂ 𝔊 is a torsion-free normal subgroup of index 24 that contains 𝔊[4]. The natural candidate is the Sanov-type subgroup {g ≡ I mod 2, diagonal entries ≡ 1 mod 4}. It is free on [[1,2],[0,1]] and [[1,0],[2,1]], has index 12 in SL(2,ℤ) and is a complement to ±1 in Γ(2). It can be read as π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, i.e. the genus-0 loop group sitting inside the genus-1 modular group.
- With this choice, 𝔊/Π_0 has order 24. The map GL(2,ℤ/4) (order 96) → 𝔊/Π_0 is the 'épimorphisme de degré 4' of the page. Its kernel is the image of Π_0 mod 4, namely {I, [[1,2],[0,1]], [[1,0],[2,1]], [[1,2],[2,1]]} ≅ (ℤ/2)^2.
- M is a profinite automorphism group (Grothendieck–Teichmüller type, genus 1) containing the profinite completion 𝔊^. It has a 'monodromy' homomorphism Θ_M : M → GL(2,ℤ̂), the action on H_1 of the punctured torus.
- ρ = e^{2πi/3}. L_ρ is the cyclic stabilizer of ρ, of order 6. D_ρ ≅ D_6 is its normalizer in GL(2,ℤ), of order 12.
- N_ρ^* ⊂ M is a normalizer-type subgroup. M^0(-j) is its smallest invariant subgroup from the previous page, of index 24.
- ε_2, ε_3 : M(0) → μ_2 are sign characters.

What the previous page established. D_ρ embeds with index 2 in N_ρ^*/M^0(-j). It also embeds with index 2 in 𝔊/Π_0, injectively because Π_0 is torsion-free.

This page. Grothendieck seeks an isomorphism N_ρ^*/M^0(-j) ≅ 𝔊/Π_0 compatible with the two embeddings of D_ρ. His Proposition:
- Let (45) be the composite M → GL(2,ℤ̂) → GL(2,ℤ/4) → 𝔊/Π_0.
- Its restriction to 𝔊^ ⊂ M is the canonical projection 𝔊^ → 𝔊^/Π_0^ = 𝔊/Π_0.
- Restricted to N_ρ^*, its kernel is exactly M^0(-j), giving (46) N_ρ^*/M^0(-j) ≅ 𝔊/Π_0.

Proof as begun here. Elements of M^0(-j) are v = α^{-1}u with u ∈ M(0), α ∈ Π_0, u(ρ) = α(ρ) (hence ε_3(u) = 1) and ε_2(u) = 1. These correspond bijectively to M^0(0) = {u ∈ M(0) : ε_2 = ε_3 = 1}.

How the next page continues. α ∈ Π_0 dies in the quotient, so v and u have the same image. The problem therefore reduces to showing that M^0(0) lies in the kernel, i.e. that (45) restricted to M(0) factors through (ε_2, ε_3) : M(0) → μ × μ. He notes that the composite M → 𝔊/Π_0 → (ℤ/4)^* ≅ ±1 equals ε_2. He also notes that the conjugation action of M on 𝔊/Π_0 induced by (45) agrees with the action of M on 𝔊 passed to the quotient (cf. his p. 599).

Strategy. Once kernel ⊇ M^0(-j) and surjectivity are known (surjectivity is clear from D_ρ together with an element outside D_ρ, or from 𝔊^ if 𝔊^ ⊂ N_ρ^*), equality follows by counting orders (24 = 24). The purpose is to identify a finite 'level-4' quotient of the stabilizer of the j = 0 point in the genus-1 automorphism group with the finite group GL(2,ℤ)/π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).
errors: The page itself contains no evident mathematical error, but the Proposition is only partially proved here. The key step (that M^0(0), equivalently M(0) modulo (ε_2,ε_3), maps trivially to 𝔊/Π_0) is deferred to the next page and flagged there with a '?' on the factorisation arrow μ×μ → 𝔊/Π_0.
Surjectivity of N_ρ^* → 𝔊/Π_0 is not addressed on this page. It is needed for (46) to be an isomorphism; the kernel computation alone gives only injectivity of the induced map.
Minor notational inconsistency: the target is written 𝔊^/Π_0 on line 2, 𝔊̂/Π_0 ≃ 𝔊̂/Π̂_0 in (45), and 𝔊/Π_0 in (46). These are all the same finite group of order 24, so this is harmless.
On the previous page the subgroup is written M^0(J) in (44) rather than M^0(-J); presumably a slip of the pen.

ideas.what: Embedding the genus-0 loop group π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) as a torsion-free, index-24, level-4 normal subgroup Π_0 of GL(2,ℤ), so that 𝔊/Π_0 is a finite group of order 24 through which genus-1 automorphism data is read.
ideas.modern_name: Sanov subgroup / Γ(2) without ±1 (level-4 congruence subgroup); Legendre covering linking genus 0 and genus 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Sanov 1947, Legendre/Jacobi level-2 structures); the genus-0/genus-1 comparison in GT theory is due to Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto and Enriquez
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the genus-1 levels of the Teichmüller tower in general terms only

ideas.what: Reducing a genus-1 monodromy homomorphism Θ_M : M → GL(2,ℤ̂) mod 4 to obtain a finite character-type invariant of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group, with the sign character ε_2 recovered as the composite to (ℤ/4)^*.
ideas.modern_name: Level-4 reduction of the genus-1 GT/Galois action on H_1 of the punctured elliptic curve

ideas.what: Identifying the finite quotient N_ρ^*/M^0(-j) of the stabilizer of the j = 0 (ρ) point with GL(2,ℤ)/Π_0, compatibly with the embeddings of the automorphism group D_ρ ≅ D_6, via a kernel computation plus an order count.
ideas.modern_name: Structure of the decomposition/inertia group at the j = 0 orbifold point in the genus-1 Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (related to Nakamura's and Ihara's analyses of the elliptic points of M_{1,1})

missed.claim: The Proposition is stated with a hesitant 'Essayons-le ainsi' and a '?' on the target isomorphism. Its key step, the factorisation of M(0) → 𝔊/Π_0 through (ε_2, ε_3), is left marked with '?' on the following page. Whether this level-4 compatibility of the genus-1 GT-type group at the j = 0 point was ever completed is unclear.
missed.quote: N_ρ^*/M^0(-j) ≃? 𝔊^/Π_0 compatible avec les plongements dans D_ρ. Essayons-le ainsi
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete finite-level compatibility statement between elliptic-point stabilizers in the genus-1 Teichmüller/GT group and the classical modular group. It could be checked against Nakamura's and Enriquez's descriptions of genus-1 GT, but it is probably a known or easy consequence of them.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in Grothendieck's genus-1 Teichmüller-tower computations: identifying a finite order-24 quotient via mod-4 reduction. It is interesting as documentation of how he linked genus 0 (Π_0 = π_1(P^1−3 points) inside GL(2,ℤ)) with genus 1 at the j = 0 point. However, the group theory is elementary, and the genus-0/genus-1 GT comparison was later developed (Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez).
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is 624 (Grothendieck's own pagination); the archive page is 642.
The underbrace in (45) labels Gl(2,ℤ) as 𝔊, i.e. GL(2,ℤ/4ℤ) ≃ 𝔊/𝔊[4]. The image shows this as a vertical ≃ under GL(2,ℤ/4ℤ), not as a separate line.
The label 'épi. de degré 4' sits above the arrow GL(2,ℤ/4ℤ) → 𝔊̂/Π_0, and the target continues '≃ 𝔊̂/Π̂_0' beneath it.
The struck-out word under 'canonique' reads 'induit' (struck) over 'composé' (struck).
M^0(-J) appears in the image with a bar or underline under J (handwritten j/J); the transcription's 'M^0(-j)' is acceptable.
